Known: a sink whose ELD stops at 48 kHz can't open E-AC-3's 192 kHz stream and mpv 0.40 stalls instead of failing, so the decision must pick PCM from the ELD (done: tests/icefin/avsim/icefin.py, 19/19 from a fresh client: the native build in the client, every profile's expect map bit-exact or PCM, the ELD re-read after every receiver change, the stale ELD in standby, unplugging without a stall; found and fixed: the decision never ran in real playback (in on_preloaded mpv's current-tracks lags the aid just set, so the codec read empty and upstream's toggles decided; the track now comes from track-list), and the ELD's rates and channels now count (E-AC-3 needs 192 kHz, TrueHD and DTS-HD 8 ch at 192 kHz), so the 48 kHz soundbar gets PCM instead of a stall; avsim.sh icefin-image builds the client disk; Linux doesn't set up the HDMI pin while the ELD is invalid (no non-audio bit, HBR left over, stock mpv alike), so (D32, the user) a receiver that isn't ready gets PCM and the playing track switches to the bitstream 4 s after it wakes, with Client Settings → Audio → Receiver in Standby to override (Always PCM, Keep Bitstream); 23/23 rows incl. the wake, a wake that drops back inside the delay, and both overrides)
